title: Do it twice
description:
A function pointer lets you pass a *function* as an argument.

Write `int applyTwice(int (*f)(int), int x)` that calls `f` on `x`, then calls `f` again on the result. With a function that adds 3, `applyTwice(addThree, 10)` is 16.

Inside `applyTwice`, call the pointer like any function: `f(x)`.
lessonTitle: Function Pointers, Callbacks and Command-Line Arguments
